study_area: Klang Valley core: Kuala Lumpur federal territory, Putrajaya federal territory, and 6 urbanised Selangor districts (Gombak, Hulu Langat, Klang, Kuala Langat, Petaling, Sepang). Deliberately excludes rural/exurban Selangor (Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor, etc.).

dosm_population.vintage: data.gov.my national series, latest row used

mlab_diurnal_curve.vintage: M-Lab NDT, aggregated over Dec 2024 onward (UTC-keyed; converted to Asia/Kuala_Lumpur at load)

sunway_qoe.vintage: Published third-party dataset, NOT self-collected — Kabeer, Nordin & Behjati (2025), 'An Urban Multi-Operator QoE-Aware Dataset for Cellular Networks in Dense Environments', Mendeley Data v1, DOI 10.17632/dx5xyyfz2y.1, published 2025-06-17. Measurements span 2024-12-03 to 2025-04-02

dosm_population_district.vintage: DOSM district population, annual series 2020-2025 (published values, in thousands)

source_vintages_note: cell_time_dataset.parquet's timestamps are a synthetic calendar window chosen so the panel overlaps the ridership file's real coverage. They are NOT the dates the underlying measurements were taken — see the per-source `vintage` fields above, which span 2020 (population) to 2026 (OSM/ridership).
panel_demo_target_warning: Do NOT report forecast skill on panel_demo_target. The hourly panel is rank-one for Ookla-anchored cells, so that label is reconstructable from (cell, hour-of-week) by memorisation. Benchmark on primary_ml_target in primary_ml_table instead.

feature_columns.note: Two different lists because same-hour QoE columns and their spatial lags are leakage when predicting the SAME hour's label, but legitimate features when predicting NEXT hour's label. See run_pipeline.get_feature_columns().

fitted_scalers.note: Min-max scalers are fitted on the earliest 80% of the panel's timestamps only, not on all rows, so a temporal-holdout model's scaler has not seen the test period. Values outside the fitted range are clipped to [0,1]. These parameters are recorded because a scaler is part of the data contract, not an implementation detail — reproduce them exactly if you re-scale downstream.

tier_guidance.measured: Real Ookla label. Show the value.
tier_guidance.estimable: No label, but inside the labelled cells' feature range. A model prediction is interpolation — show it with a confidence caveat.
tier_guidance.unknown: No label and outside common support. A prediction is extrapolation into unseen territory. Present as 'insufficient data' rather than as a number — an honest gap reads better than a confident guess.

coverage_bias.interpretation: An AUC well above 0.5 means Ookla coverage is predictable from GIS features, so training on labelled cells and predicting unlabelled ones is extrapolation. Weight by coverage_propensity and flag predictions outside common support.

application_profiles.threshold_source: Engineering guidance — ITU-T G.114 one-way delay for interactive speech, typical codec and streaming throughput requirements. NOT derived from any survey.
application_profiles.weight_source: MCMC Broadband Quality of Experience Survey 2024, mobile broadband results. Used ONLY to weight how much each application failure matters to Malaysian users — never to set a technical threshold.
application_profiles.known_gap: Ookla provides download, upload and latency but NOT jitter or packet loss. Voice and video-call profiles are therefore partial and optimistic: a cell can meet every measurable criterion and still deliver choppy audio. app_n_evaluable records how many criteria were actually checkable per row.

voice_call.label: Online voice calls
voice_call.driver: latency, jitter and loss — throughput is almost irrelevant
voice_call.top_user_complaint: choppy or broken voice (49.0% of dissatisfied users)

web_browsing.label: Web browsing
web_browsing.driver: latency first — a page load is many round trips — then throughput

video_call.label: Online video calls
video_call.driver: throughput and jitter together, in both directions

online_gaming.label: Online gaming
online_gaming.driver: latency above all; bandwidth needs are tiny

high_leakage_risk_features.demand_pressure_index: Circular with the simulated QoE generator via its historical_qoe component (lag_24h_rtt_median). Use demand_pressure_base instead for a non-circular, real-data-only feature.
high_leakage_risk_features.qoe_level_is_ookla_anchored: Near-perfectly determines whether target_is_degraded_next_1h can be positive at all on the simulated panel — see run_full_validation's validate_target_anchor_correlation warning for the current split. Excluded from the default feature list, not just flagged.
high_leakage_risk_features.qoe_baseline_source: Human-readable restatement of qoe_level_is_ookla_anchored — same exclusion reason.
high_leakage_risk_features.ookla_quarter_test_count: Only non-null when qoe_level_is_ookla_anchored is True — a direct proxy for anchor status, same exclusion reason.
high_leakage_risk_features.ookla_quarter_device_count: Only non-null when qoe_level_is_ookla_anchored is True — a direct proxy for anchor status, same exclusion reason.
high_leakage_risk_features.ookla_dl_mbps: This IS the Option A modelling target — never a feature.
high_leakage_risk_features.ookla_rtt_ms: This IS the Option A modelling target — never a feature.
high_leakage_risk_features.ookla_tests: Real quarterly Ookla sample count — target-adjacent, never a feature.
high_leakage_risk_features.ookla_devices: Real quarterly Ookla device count — target-adjacent, never a feature.
high_leakage_risk_features.has_real_ookla_label: Split indicator (labelled vs. prediction-target cells), not a predictor — training on it would leak which rows have a real label.
high_leakage_risk_features.qoe_risk_label: Directly thresholded from ookla_dl_mbps (the target) — using it as a feature reads the answer off a relabelled copy of itself.
high_leakage_risk_features.ookla_is_synthetic: has_real_ookla_label inverted under a different name — same exclusion reason.

simulation_disclosure.explanation: cell_time_dataset.parquet is a hierarchical panel, not a measurement: a REAL citywide hourly shape (M-Lab NDT) applied to a REAL per-cell level (Ookla quarterly) where one exists, and to a formula-derived level where it does not. Jitter, loss and upload remain simulated. No per-cell per-hour QoE measurement source exists for this project. Because one shape is shared by every cell, the anchored panel is rank-one and its forecast target is analytically reconstructable — see PANEL_STRUCTURE_DISCLOSURE before reporting any forecast metric. For a modelling claim that stands up to review, use cell_static_qoe_baseline.parquet (real Ookla targets, real GIS features, zero synthetic QoE).

per_component_provenance.hourly_shape_dl_rtt: REAL — M-Lab NDT citywide diurnal curve (2.05M tests), keyed in UTC in the source CSV and converted to Asia/Kuala_Lumpur at load. ONE curve applied uniformly to every cell: a real shape, not per-cell resolution. Traffic mix not ASN-filtered, so it may include fixed as well as mobile tests.
per_component_provenance.hourly_level_dl_rtt_anchored_cells: REAL — the cell's own Ookla 2024 Q4 quarterly average, used as the level the real hourly shape is applied to.
per_component_provenance.hourly_level_dl_rtt_unanchored_cells: FORMULA-DERIVED — no Ookla tile coverage exists for these cells, so the level comes from a population/POI load function plus seeded Gaussian noise. Flagged per row by qoe_level_is_ookla_anchored.
per_component_provenance.hourly_jitter_loss_ul: SIMULATED — no free real source exists at this resolution. Sparse real ping/jitter/loss values (0.2% coverage) exist only inside the Sunway inset and are kept separately, never merged into these.

simulation_disclosure.recommended_defensible_dataset: cell_static_qoe_baseline.parquet (real Ookla labels only, zero simulated values)

panel_structure_disclosure.explanation: For Ookla-anchored cells the hourly panel is exactly ookla_static(cell) x mlab_curve(hour-of-week), deterministic and rank-one: every anchored cell shares ONE identical temporal curve, differing only in level. Consequences the modelling team must know: (1) target_is_degraded_next_1h is fully determined by (cell, hour-of-week), so a model given cell identity and time recovers it by memorisation — reported forecast skill on this panel is not evidence of real predictive ability; (2) there is no cell-specific temporal dynamics, so no model can learn that one area degrades earlier than another, because that information is not present; (3) Getis-Ord Gi* is invariant to a global scale factor, so hotspot recurrence varies only through the Gaussian noise injected into unanchored cells — 'this area degraded in N of the last 7 evenings' is not currently supportable. Fixing this requires a spatially-varying real diurnal curve (per-district M-Lab), not a modelling change.
panel_structure_disclosure.verified_reconstruction: dl/rtt for Ookla-anchored cells reconstruct from ookla_static x mlab_curve with max absolute error 0.0, and the reconstructed degradation target matches the stored target on 100% of anchored rows.

known_limitations: No per-CELL per-hour QoE measurement source exists for this study area. cell_time_dataset.parquet combines a REAL citywide hourly shape (M-Lab NDT, converted from UTC to Asia/Kuala_Lumpur at load) with a REAL per-cell level (Ookla quarterly) where tile coverage exists, and a formula-derived level where it does not. Jitter, packet loss and upload remain simulated. Because ONE shape is shared by every cell, the anchored panel is rank-one — see panel_structure_disclosure before reporting any forecast metric from it.

The M-Lab curve is a single CITY-WIDE curve and was not ASN-filtered, so it may mix fixed-broadband and mobile tests. Per-district curves (which would break the rank-one structure) require re-querying M-Lab grouped by client geolocation.

No real network capacity/traffic/utilisation data exists. demand_pressure_* features are exposure/activity PROXIES, not a measurement of actual load vs. capacity — do not claim 'confirmed congestion', only 'QoE degradation associated with estimated demand pressure'.

Study area is Klang Valley core: Kuala Lumpur federal territory, Putrajaya federal territory, and 6 urbanised Selangor districts (Gombak, Hulu Langat, Klang, Kuala Langat, Petaling, Sepang). Deliberately excludes rural/exurban Selangor (Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor, etc.).

On the SIMULATED hourly panel (cell_time_dataset.parquet), positive target_is_degraded_next_1h labels are concentrated in Ookla-anchored cells — see run_full_validation's validate_target_anchor_correlation warnings for the exact current split. qoe_level_is_ookla_anchored can be a near-trivial predictor of the target on this simulated panel; report metrics split by anchor status, or restrict training/eval to anchored cells, rather than trusting one aggregate PR-AUC.
tower_count is a deduplicated approximation of physical sites (rounding-based clustering of OpenCellID records), not an authoritative operator site inventory.
target_qoe_index / target_service_quality_1to5 are a custom composite index, not a validated ITU-T G.107 E-model MOS.

h3_parent_res6 (res-6 H3 parent, ~130 groups over the current grid) is provided on every output table for SPATIAL HOLDOUT splits — group by it and hold out whole groups; do not randomly sample individual h3_index rows for a test set, spatially neighbouring res-8 cells are autocorrelated and a random split will leak.
